concepts.name: Tibetan Plateau
concepts.definition: The world's highest and largest plateau, spanning roughly 2.5 million km² mainly in China with an average elevation above 4,500 m; the "Roof of the World."

concepts.name: Deccan Plateau
concepts.definition: Large plateau covering about 422,000 km² across southern India, bounded by the Eastern and Western Ghats and averaging around 600 m in elevation.

concepts.name: Iranian Plateau
concepts.definition: Vast mountainous plateau spanning West, Central and South Asia, stretching ~2,000 km from the Caspian Sea to Pakistan and covering most of Iran, all of Afghanistan and western Pakistan.

concepts.name: Anatolian Plateau
concepts.definition: Semi-arid interior plateau occupying most of Turkey, rising from about 600 m in the west to 1,200 m and enclosed by folded mountain ranges to north and south.

concepts.name: Mongolian Plateau
concepts.definition: High interior basin of Inner Asia ringed by the Altai to the west, the Sayan and Khentii to the north, the Greater Hinggan to the east and the Yin Mountains to the south; the map shows its core in Mongolia, while the term is often stretched to take in Inner Mongolia, the Gobi and the Russian Transbaikal.

concepts.name: Mexican Plateau
concepts.definition: Large arid-to-semiarid plateau covering much of northern and central Mexico, averaging ~1,825 m and flanked by the Sierra Madre Occidental and Sierra Madre Oriental.

concepts.name: Colorado Plateau
concepts.definition: High semi-arid plateau of about 340,000 km² centred on the Four Corners region of the U.S. Southwest, spanning Utah, Arizona, Colorado and New Mexico and drained mostly by the Colorado River.

concepts.name: Altiplano
concepts.definition: High plateau of the central Andes in west-central South America, the most extensive high plateau outside Tibet, averaging ~3,750 m across Bolivia, Peru, Chile and Argentina.

concepts.name: Brazilian Highlands
concepts.definition: Extensive eroded plateau covering the eastern, southern and central portions of Brazil, roughly half the country's area, rising to Pico da Bandeira at 2,891 m.

concepts.name: Amazon Basin
concepts.definition: The ~7-million-km² region of South America drained by the Amazon River across eight countries, holding the world's largest and most biodiverse tropical rainforest.

concepts.name: Congo Basin
concepts.definition: The ~3.7-million-km² drainage basin of the Congo River in Central Africa, containing the world's second-largest rainforest and spanning nine countries.
